# DREAMS in manifoldsR

The t-SNE vignette has a warning in it: distances between clusters mean
nothing. Two blobs sitting next to each other might be miles apart in the input
space. PCA has the opposite problem. The global layout is faithful, but
everything local gets squashed into an overlapping mess.

DREAMS sits in between. It is t-SNE with an extra pull towards a global
reference embedding, PCA by default. You keep the clusters of t-SNE and their
positions relative to each other start meaning something again. Original work
by Kury, Kobak & Damrich, Transactions on Machine Learning Research, 2026.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(manifoldsR)
library(magrittr)
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
```

## Intro

Every t-SNE epoch, DREAMS scales the usual update by `1 - lambda` and adds a
quadratic pull towards the reference:

$$-\eta \lambda^2 \frac{2}{n} (y - \alpha y_e)$$

$y_e$ is the centred reference, $\alpha = \|Y\|_F / \|Y_e\|_F$ rescales it to
the current size of the embedding, and $\eta$ is the automatic openTSNE
learning rate. The optimisation starts from the reference too, so the
`init` element of `params_tsne()` is ignored.

One knob, set via `params_dreams()`:

- `lambda`. Regularisation strength in `[0, 1]`. `0` is t-SNE (started from
  the reference), `1` returns the reference. Defaults to `0.15`, the value
  from the paper.

The regulariser is `O(n)` per epoch on top of the Barnes-Hut or FFT repulsion,
so DREAMS costs about what t-SNE costs. Every `approx_type` from `tsne()`
works here as well.

## Measuring both ends

We need two numbers per embedding. Global: the Spearman correlation between
subcluster centroid distances in the input and in the embedding. Local: the
fraction of each point's 15 nearest neighbours that survive the embedding.

```{r}
#| label: metric helpers
global_preservation <- function(data, embd, membership) {
  centroids <- function(x) {
    split(seq_len(nrow(x)), membership) %>%
      lapply(\(i) colMeans(x[i, , drop = FALSE])) %>%
      do.call(rbind, .)
  }
  cor(
    as.vector(dist(centroids(data))),
    as.vector(dist(centroids(embd))),
    method = "spearman"
  )
}

knn_preservation <- function(data, embd, k = 15L) {
  idx <- function(x) {
    generate_knn_graph(
      data = x,
      k = k,
      knn_method = "exhaustive",
      .verbose = FALSE
    ) %>%
      get_idx_mat()
  }
  idx_data <- idx(data)
  idx_embd <- idx(embd)
  mean(vapply(
    seq_len(nrow(idx_data)),
    \(i) length(intersect(idx_data[i, ], idx_embd[i, ])) / k,
    numeric(1)
  ))
}
```

The hierarchical generator gives us 16 subclusters, grouped into 4
supergroups, in 50 dimensions. Subclusters within a supergroup are close,
supergroups are far apart. Exactly the structure t-SNE throws away.

```{r}
#| label: synthetic data
hierarchical_data <- manifold_synthetic_data(
  type = "hierarchical",
  n_samples = 5000L,
  dim = 50L,
  parameters = params_hierarchical(n_supergroups = 4L, n_subclusts = 4L)
)

subgroup <- hierarchical_data$membership$subgroup
supergroup <- hierarchical_data$membership$supergroup
```

## PCA vs t-SNE vs DREAMS

```{r}
#| label: pca tsne dreams
pca_res <- prcomp(hierarchical_data$data, rank. = 2)$x

tsne_res <- tsne(
  data = hierarchical_data$data,
  seed = 42L,
  .verbose = FALSE
)

dreams_res <- dreams(
  data = hierarchical_data$data,
  seed = 42L,
  .verbose = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| label: pca tsne dreams plot
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.5
embeddings <- list(PCA = pca_res, tSNE = tsne_res, DREAMS = dreams_res)

plot_df <- lapply(embeddings, \(embd) {
  data.table(
    dim1 = embd[, 1],
    dim2 = embd[, 2],
    supergroup = as.factor(supergroup),
    subgroup = as.factor(subgroup)
  )
}) %>%
  rbindlist(idcol = "method") %>%
  .[, method := factor(method, levels = names(embeddings))]

ggplot(
  data = plot_df,
  mapping = aes(x = dim1, y = dim2)
) +
  geom_point(
    mapping = aes(colour = supergroup, shape = subgroup),
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 0.75
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = rep(c(16, 17, 15, 3), 4), guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~method, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw() +
  xlab("Dim 1") +
  ylab("Dim 2") +
  ggtitle("Hierarchical data, coloured by supergroup")
```

PCA gets the four supergroups in the right places and smears the subclusters
within them. t-SNE separates all 16 subclusters cleanly, and then scatters
them over the plane with no regard for which supergroup they belong to.
DREAMS keeps the 16 subclusters separated and keeps each supergroup together.

```{r}
#| label: pca tsne dreams metrics
lapply(embeddings, \(embd) {
  data.table(
    global = global_preservation(hierarchical_data$data, embd, subgroup),
    local = knn_preservation(hierarchical_data$data, embd)
  )
}) %>%
  rbindlist(idcol = "method") %>%
  .[, lapply(.SD, round, 3), by = method]
```

The numbers say the same thing. DREAMS matches PCA on the global score and
keeps most of the kNN preservation of t-SNE. PCA's local score is dismal: two
dimensions out of fifty is not enough to keep anyone's neighbours.

## Tuning lambda

`lambda` trades one end against the other. A sweep from t-SNE to PCA:

```{r}
#| label: lambda sweep
lambdas <- c(0, 0.05, 0.15, 0.5, 1)

lambda_sweep <- lapply(lambdas, \(lambda) {
  dreams(
    data = hierarchical_data$data,
    dreams_params = params_dreams(lambda = lambda),
    seed = 42L,
    .verbose = FALSE
  )
})
names(lambda_sweep) <- sprintf("lambda = %.2f", lambdas)

lapply(lambda_sweep, \(embd) {
  data.table(
    global = global_preservation(hierarchical_data$data, embd, subgroup),
    local = knn_preservation(hierarchical_data$data, embd)
  )
}) %>%
  rbindlist(idcol = "lambda") %>%
  .[, lapply(.SD, round, 3), by = lambda]
```

```{r}
#| label: lambda sweep plot
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 8
sweep_df <- lapply(lambda_sweep, \(embd) {
  data.table(
    dim1 = embd[, 1],
    dim2 = embd[, 2],
    supergroup = as.factor(supergroup)
  )
}) %>%
  rbindlist(idcol = "lambda") %>%
  .[, lambda := factor(lambda, levels = names(lambda_sweep))]

ggplot(
  data = sweep_df,
  mapping = aes(x = dim1, y = dim2)
) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(colour = supergroup), alpha = 0.5, size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~lambda, scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
  theme_bw() +
  xlab("Dim 1") +
  ylab("Dim 2") +
  ggtitle("DREAMS lambda sweep")
```

Even `0.05` buys most of the global structure back. The local score holds up
to the default and then drops off fast. Past `0.5` you are looking at a
slightly sharpened PCA. At `1` nothing moves at all: you get the reference at
its initialisation scale (note the `1e-04` axes). The default is a sensible
place to start; go lower if the subclusters start to touch.

## Bring your own reference

PCA is a fine reference when the global structure is linear-ish. When it is
not, hand DREAMS something better via `reference`: any samples x 2 matrix
works, e.g. a PHATE or MDS embedding. On branching trajectory data PHATE is
the obvious pick.

```{r}
#| label: trajectory data
trajectory_data <- manifold_synthetic_data(
  type = "trajectory",
  n_samples = 5000L
)

phate_traj <- phate(
  data = trajectory_data$data,
  k = 15L,
  seed = 42L,
  .verbose = FALSE
)

tsne_traj <- tsne(
  data = trajectory_data$data,
  seed = 42L,
  .verbose = FALSE
)

dreams_traj <- dreams(
  data = trajectory_data$data,
  reference = phate_traj,
  seed = 42L,
  .verbose = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| label: trajectory plot
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.5
traj_embeddings <- list(
  PHATE = phate_traj,
  tSNE = tsne_traj,
  `DREAMS (PHATE reference)` = dreams_traj
)

traj_df <- lapply(traj_embeddings, \(embd) {
  data.table(
    dim1 = embd[, 1],
    dim2 = embd[, 2],
    branch = as.factor(trajectory_data$membership)
  )
}) %>%
  rbindlist(idcol = "method") %>%
  .[, method := factor(method, levels = names(traj_embeddings))]

ggplot(
  data = traj_df,
  mapping = aes(x = dim1, y = dim2)
) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(colour = branch), alpha = 0.5, size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~method, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw() +
  xlab("Dim 1") +
  ylab("Dim 2") +
  ggtitle("Trajectory data, coloured by branch")
```

Mixed bag. The branch order along the main stem follows PHATE, where t-SNE
just piles branches 3 and 5 on top of each other. But the long PHATE tips of
branches 2 and 5 tear off into separate islands. Long, stretched references
look like the hard case here.

Already have a `NearestNeighbours` object? Pass it via `knn =` and DREAMS
skips the search, same as every other method in the package.
